Class LocalMustAliasAnalysis

java.lang.Object
sootup.analysis.intraprocedural.LocalMustAliasAnalysis
Direct Known Subclasses:
StrongLocalMustAliasAnalysis
public class LocalMustAliasAnalysis extends Object
Intraprocedural must-alias analysis for locals of reference type, ported from Soot's LocalMustAliasAnalysis.

Every local is mapped to a value number before each statement: this and the parameters have fixed numbers, every other right-hand side (e.g. an allocation or a method call) gets a number of its own, and copies propagate the number. Where two branches assign different numbers to a local, the local gets a number that is unique to that merge point, so that copies made after the merge are still recognized as aliases. Two locals must-alias at a statement if they have the same number before it.

A number assigned inside a loop stands for the objects of all iterations, so two locals with that number may refer to objects of different iterations; StrongLocalMustAliasAnalysis discards such numbers.
